answer: The network records each agent’s reputation as a continuously flowing river of credit, incremented only when the agent completes verifiable tasks and signed attestations. Reputation ages like a violet hue that deepens over time but fades if the agent stops to wander, requiring periodic proof‑of‑work stamps that cost computational tokens each cycle. An attacker must forge enough fresh stamps and sustain the token expense to mimic the long‑standing flow, making a Sybil attack economically prohibitive.
